7.text: The Maritime Chukchee call themselves and other maritime people añqaˊlɪt

8.text: (“sea people”), from aˊñqᴀ (“the sea”); or ramaˊg̣lat (“seacoast dwellers”).

9.text: In distinction from other alien tribes, both Reindeer and Maritime Chukchee

10.text: call themselves lɪˊi-yiˊlɪlɪt (“those of genuine language”), also oraˊwêʟ̣at (“men”)

11.text: or lɪˊê-oraˊwêʟ̣at (“genuine men”), in the same way as the Asiatic Eskimo

12.text: call themselves Yuˊɪt or Yu-piˊɪt (yuk, “man;” yu-pi, “genuine man”). The

13.text: people of the alien tribes are called by the Chukchee aˊlva-yêˊlɪlɪt (“those of

14.text: alien language”). All other names used by various writers in connection with

15.text: the Chukchee tribe are for the most part the result of misunderstanding.

16.text: Thus the assertion of so many travellers, from Krasheninnikoff to Bog-

17.text: danovitch, that the maritime inhabitants of the Chukchee or Koryak shores

18.text: call themselves also Čauˊču, shows only that the people with whom they

19.text: conversed, though following maritime pursuits to some extent, were originally

20.text: of Reindeer stock, and probably still had some herds farther inland. The

23.text: The name Tuski, adopted by W. H. Hooper with the strange explanation

24.text: that it means a confederation or brotherhood, has probably arisen from an

25.text: attempt to simplify the misspelling Tchuski instead of Tchukotski (Чукотскій),

26.text: the Russian adjective from the substantive Tchukcha (Чукча, “Chukchee”).

27.text: Hooper writes Tchutskoi Noss instead of Tchukotskiy Noss (“Chukotsky Cape”). ¹

28.text: The name Chukmari, adopted by A. A. Resin for a tribe “intermediary

29.text: between the Koryak and the Chukchee,”² is derived from the popular Kamchatkan

30.text: term for the Chukchee, Chukhmaryo (Чухмарье). He gives this name to the

31.text: people living on the Opukski and Tumanski coasts; i. e., respectively to the

32.text: Kerek and the Telqäˊp Reindeer Chukchee, who are in reality the rudest and

33.text: most primitive branches of the Koryak and the Chukchee tribes.
